history.formed: First B-24 arrived Seething Airfield 25 November 1943
history.summary: The 448th Bombardment Group (Heavy) flew B-24 Liberators from Seething Airfield in Norfolk from late 1943 through to the end of the war in Europe. The group's first mission was flown on 22 December 1943 and its last on 25 April 1945, completing 262 missions and 6,774 sorties during which 15,272 tons of bombs were dropped. 101 aircraft were lost in action and 499 men were killed in training and operations. The former control tower at Seething is now a museum, open to the public on the first Sunday of each month from May to October. Two memorials mark the group — a black marble tablet at the former airfield site and a second at St Margaret and St Remigius Church, Seething.
